column7: As Christendom today is divided into separate sects, denominations, or belief structures, so too, were the Jews of Jesus' age divided. During the time of Jesus, four major Jewish sects shaped the religious and political landscape of Israel, each with distinct beliefs and expectations about the Messiah. Understanding some background on these different groups can help provide meaningful context to a study of the New Testament scriptures.

column7: The purpose of Jesus ministry and service was both individual and global, immediate, and long lasting. His purpose does not have a singular focus but is part of God’s divine plan to reconcile humanity to God. After sin entered the world, it caused a division between God and mankind. God had to banish man from the garden and from His presence. Throughout the Old Testament, man could be with God, but only partially. It was very rare that God's spirit was given to men, and in the large part men lived in isolation from God. He found a people in the Jews, but wanted a permanent, sure, and complete way to restore His relationship with mankind.
column8: Jesus’ mission and ministry were personal yet global, immediate yet long-term. His purpose did not have a single focus, but was part of God’s divine plan to reconcile humanity to God. After sin entered the world, a division arose between God and man. God had no choice but to banish humanity from the garden and from His presence. Throughout the Old Testament, people could be with God, but only in part. It was exceedingly rare for the Spirit of God to be given to people, and most people lived in a state of separation from God. God found His people among the Jews, but He desired a permanent, certain, and complete way to restore relationship with humankind.
